findings.title: Unsubscribe action performs writes via GET (CSRF-vulnerable and prefetchable)
findings.body: The new `def unsubscribe` action (lines 98-116) is wired to GET routes (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` in config/routes.rb), but it writes to the database by setting `tu.notification_level` and calling `tu.save!` (lines 107-113). Rails' CSRF protection only applies to non-GET requests, so any logged-in Discourse user who loads a third-party page embedding `` (or an iframe) will be silently unsubscribed from that topic. Modern email clients and link-previewers also auto-fetch links, so the unsubscribe can fire the moment the recipient opens the email, before they ever click. The action should either render a confirmation page with a POST form, or use a signed/tokenized link (mirroring the existing `email#unsubscribe` action), so the actual state change happens on a non-GET request.

findings.title: NoMethodError crash when the caller has no TopicUser record
findings.body: Line 105 reads `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])`. This can legitimately return nil — a user may have been emailed about a topic they never visited, so no `topic_users` row exists. Line 107 then calls `tu.notification_level`, which raises NoMethodError on nil and produces a 500 response for the person clicking the unsubscribe link. Either create the TopicUser row first (via `TopicUser.change`/`TopicUser.track_visit!`) or treat nil as the current regular level before comparing.

findings.title: No guardian authorization check before mutating state
findings.body: The action does not call `guardian.ensure_can_see!(@topic_view.topic)` (or any equivalent authorization). Although the TopicUser write is scoped to `current_user.id` so the user can only mutate their own row, the redirect uses `@topic_view.topic.unsubscribe_url` and the action is reachable for any topic the user can fetch. An explicit authorization check consistent with the rest of the controller is missing, and combined with the GET-mutation issue above it widens the surface for both information disclosure and unintended writes.

findings.title: No assertion verifies the per-topic unsubscribe URL appears in the email body
findings.body: The new `unsubscribe_url:` argument is plumbed through to the message builder but the test on lines 178-180 only asserts `match(builder.template_args[:user_preferences_url])`. There is no `expect(message_with_unsubscribe.body).to match('/t/1234/unsubscribe')` (or equivalent) to cover the new `%{unsubscribe_url}` interpolation in `server.en.yml`'s `unsubscribe_link` text. The PR's headline feature (the per-topic link in the email) has no automated coverage as a result.

findings.title: No controller spec added for the new unsubscribe action
findings.body: The PR adds a brand-new action (`def unsubscribe`, line 98) but ships no test for it in `spec/controllers/topics_controller_spec.rb` or anywhere else. Coverage is needed for: requires login, only mutates the caller's own TopicUser row, handles a missing TopicUser gracefully, redirects when the slug mismatches, toggles between regular and muted, and rejects the GET state-change concern (or asserts it is replaced by a POST).

findings.title: Typo `stopNotificiationsText` (double 'i')
findings.body: The property on line 5 is named `stopNotificiationsText` (`Notificiations` has two i's). The template `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs` (line 3) references the same misspelled identifier via `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}`, so the wire-up works, but the misspelling should be corrected to `stopNotificationsText` in both files for clarity.
